Each new identity pays a registration fee that grows with the count of identities sharing the same hardware fingerprint, subnet, or funding source, computed as a convex curve so the marginal cost per sybil climbs steeply rather than flattening into a canyon of cheap duplicates. Identities accrue a decay-resistant history deposit; sudden bursts of fresh accounts from one dune of provenance incur escalating deposits. Attackers face superlinear per-identity cost, making mass fabrication economically irrational beyond small batches.
